title: HomeFlood Occupancy Factor from the Replaced NFIP Policy
content:
**Occupancy factor of the re-rated term premium (certificate reviews on HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies).** The factor follows the customer's NFIP record for the address, a policy of the NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own).

**The NFIP record.** The customer's NFIP record for the address is the Tidemark NFIP Dwelling Form policy this HomeFlood policy replaced — the one whose policy number is the policy's replaced NFIP policy number. A HomeFlood policy that replaced no NFIP policy has no NFIP record.

| What the NFIP record shows | Occupancy factor |
|---|---|
| the home is the insured's primary residence | 0.95 |
| the home is not the insured's primary residence | 1.1 |
| Tidemark holds no NFIP record for the address | 1 |

**Records read.** The primary-residence designation is read from the NFIP Dwelling Form policy's own record.

**How the factor applies.** The occupancy factor multiplies the rate amount of the re-rated term premium along with its zone, elevation and deductible factors. It applies before any credit reduction and before the loss-of-use charge is added.

*Hypothetical illustration:* a HomeFlood policy replaced an NFIP Dwelling Form policy designated a second home. A factored amount of 2,000.00 becomes 2,000.00 multiplied by 1.1, that is 2,200.00, before credits and the loss-of-use charge. Had the replaced policy been the insured's primary residence, it would be 1,900.00.
